title: Batavia massacre of ethnic Chinese
summary: In October 1740 Chinese residents of Batavia, the Dutch East India Company's Asian headquarters, were massacred in a pogrom. Historian Leonard Blussé links it to a revolt by Chinese peasants in the hinterland and says about a third of the city burned; a popular account puts the Chinese dead above 10,000.

uncertainty.note: Harvard Asia Center gives 9 to 11 October 1740 for the slaughter of Chinese inside the city; The China Project dates the start to 9 October and says the violence went on for nearly two weeks, so the end date is approximate.

as_recorded.value: This went on for nearly two weeks

when.display: From 9 October 1740 (core killing 9-11 October; violence lasted nearly two weeks)

where.modern_name: Kota Tua (Old Town), Jakarta, Indonesia (Batavia was the walled city; the violence also spread to the surrounding countryside)
where.historical_name: Batavia, headquarters of the Dutch East India Company in Asia, Java

importance.justification: A mass killing of the Chinese community in the Dutch East India Company's Asian capital.

audience_note: This record describes the mass killing of civilians. Death-toll figures are estimates and vary by source.

sources.title: The Colonization of Batavia and the Massacre of 1740 (event abstract by Leonard Blussé)

reviewer_note: Least sure of the death toll: the China Project says more than 10,000 Chinese died, while the Harvard abstract gives no figure, so the toll appears only as a popular estimate. The Leiden University Press page could not be opened and is not cited. The pin is the old walled city, not a street-level site.
